- Any constraints on payload size or rate limits for webhook-batched requests?

Hi Alex — great to hear from you, and thanks for signing up.

Short answers up front:
- Integration pattern: yes — we often see an Actions runner POST to a small edge service that fans requests to Redwood; we support both sync generation and async callbacks.
- Auth: for CI/runner use cases we typically recommend a scoped machine token (service account) with a short TTL if you want extra safety; we also support customer-managed HMAC headers for webhook verification.
- Payloads/rate limits: payload size is fine for typical Action outputs (up to ~512KB); for large payloads we recommend uploading artifacts and passing references. Rate limits depend on plan and model; for demos we can show batching and KV caching to reduce volume.

I'd be happy to set up a 30-minute walkthrough and show an example Action + small demo repo. Are any of these slots next week OK for you (all PT):
- Mon 3/2 2:00pm
- Tue 3/3 11:00am
- Wed 3/4 4:00pm

If none of those work, tell me a couple times and we'll pivot. Priyom (copied) will join to cover security and deployment options (Private/VPC). I'm attaching a one-pager that covers typical OSS patterns.

Attachment: redwood-demo-onepager.pdf (application/pdf, 280 KB)

Best,
Marissa
